records.availability: Public HackerOne bounty program active; no pause banner observed.
in_scope_assets: Recon Data (official ListDomains and ListIPs endpoints)
scope_conditions: The ubereats wildcard excludes every separately listed out-of-scope host.
Recon data is informational and does not make every returned asset bounty-eligible.
Reports must contain analysis, validation, reasoning and demonstrable security impact rather than scanner output.
Researchers may test only accounts they own and must minimize any access to other users' data.
records.automation: Automated scan and enumeration reports without additional analysis, validation, reasoning and demonstrated impact are excluded. The policy does not establish permission for ScopeGuard's unattended production checks.
records.request_limit_note: No numerical testing request limit found in the official policy or scope table read. Null means unknown, not unlimited.
records.accounts: Owned test accounts are required. The program expects a HackerOne testing identity using the @wearehackerone.com alias; no preconfigured account was provided or created.
excluded_assets: merchants.ubereats.com (same-organization role escalation; cross-tenant issues remain eligible)
exclusions: Brute force, denial of service, social engineering and destructive testing
Automated output without manual validation and impact
Missing headers, TLS configuration, open ports, banners and versions without a security exploit
Rate-limit observations without demonstrated security impact
Accessing or changing other users' data beyond the minimum proof
unresolved: No permission for the proposed autonomous header checks was established.
No numerical request limit was published in the pages reviewed.
A future manual test would still need an exact eligible asset, owned account and reportable impact hypothesis.
records.note: Active public program, but the reviewed rules require controlled, identified and manually validated research. No target activated.
records.evidence_method: Official public HackerOne policy and rendered scope table
records.live_directory_membership: Not verified: authenticated ScopeGuard state unavailable

records.availability: Public HackerOne bounty program active with open scope across Superhuman, Grammarly and Coda products.
scope_conditions: Third-party SaaS domains reached through Superhuman wildcards are excluded.
The same Grammarly extension vulnerability across browsers is treated as one report.
Capture the Flag is governed by its own challenge instructions.
Real customer accounts must not be used; doing so may reduce an otherwise eligible bounty.
records.automation: Automated scanner output without manual validation is out of scope. Crash dumps or tool output alone are insufficient. The policy does not establish permission for unattended ScopeGuard checks.
records.request_limit_note: No numerical testing request limit found in the official policy or scope table read. Null means unknown, not unlimited.
records.accounts: Owned test accounts are required. Coda permits up to five free-plan accounts using a HackerOne alias or hackeronetester identifier. Grammarly and Superhuman require a HackerOne-style testing identity; Superhuman Mail requires an owned Google or Outlook workspace. No account or paid upgrade was created.
exclusions: Denial of service, stress testing and disruption
Automated scanner output without manual validation
Missing headers, open ports, banners and versions without demonstrated impact
Third-party SaaS, packs, agents and integrations not operated by the program
AI prompt injection or jailbreaks without a security boundary impact
Trial, referral or billing abuse
Account enumeration and rate-limit-only reports without demonstrated impact
unresolved: No permission for the proposed autonomous header checks was established.
No numerical request limit was published in the pages reviewed.
Product-specific test identity and account setup remain prerequisites for any future manual work.
records.note: Active public program with exact scope, but owned test accounts and manual validation are required. No target activated.
records.evidence_method: Official public HackerOne policy and rendered scope table
records.live_directory_membership: Not verified: authenticated ScopeGuard state unavailable

records.availability: Public HackerOne Web2 bounty program active; Web3 issues are directed to a separate Cantina program.
in_scope_assets: Other Coinbase-operated applications missed by the standard scope (bounty-ineligible; reviewed individually)
scope_conditions: Only High and Critical Web2 findings are bounty-eligible; Low and Medium findings receive no bounty.
The special Extreme category applies to compromise of hot/cold-wallet funds or private keys.
cb-mpc-go and the catch-all Other row are explicitly bounty-ineligible.
Demo, testnet and staging environments are excluded.
records.automation: No explicit permission for automated or unattended testing was found in the official pages reviewed. Directory inclusion and wildcard scope do not provide that permission.
records.request_limit_note: No numerical testing request limit found in the official policy or scope table read. Null means unknown, not unlimited.
records.accounts: No explicit public test-account or testing-identity instructions were found in the pages reviewed. Account requirements therefore remain unresolved, not approved.
excluded_assets: N/A - assets not owned or operated by Coinbase
exclusions: Low and Medium severity findings
Social engineering, physical attacks and username enumeration
Non-critical rate limiting
Deprecated libraries without demonstrated exploitability
Third-party applications that integrate with Coinbase
ACH, chargeback or other banking-system abuse
Rotated or invalid leaked credentials
Demo, testnet and staging assets
